did_you_know.text: The verse describes the outpouring of the Lord’s Spirit on “all flesh”—an expression emphasizing the broad scope of the promise and the fact that it is not limited to a small group.
The prophecy mentions the sons and daughters of Israel, the elderly and the young: the sons and daughters will prophesy, the elderly will dream dreams, and the young men will see visions.
The promise also includes male and female servants. In this way, the text presents the Lord’s Spirit as a gift given to people from every social class.
The expression “in those days” connects the outpouring of the Spirit with a future time described in the prophecy, rather than with an ordinary event in daily life.
Before the day of the Lord, signs are described both in the heavens and on the earth, including blood, fire, and columns of smoke.

The prophecy describes changes in the heavenly lights: the sun will be turned to darkness and the moon to blood. These are presented as signs that will occur before the coming of the great and awe-inspiring day of the Lord.
The verse presents calling on the name of the Lord as connected with escape: “everyone who calls on the name of the Lord” will escape.
Mount Zion and Jerusalem are described as places where there will be deliverance, and “the survivors” whom the Lord calls are also mentioned.
